newsitem.title: USA: Sports Illustrated to publish magazine for women.
newsitem.headline: Sports Illustrated to publish magazine for women.

text.p: Sports Illustrated will publish a sports magazine for women in April 1997, Sports Illustrated President Don Elliman said Monday.
The new magazine, with the working title "Sports Illustrated Woman," will be published by Sports Illustrated twice in 1997, with the frequency to be determined for 1998 and beyond.
"The biggest market that we don't speak to directly is women. We would like to change that," Elliman said.

Targeted to the "Title IX generation" -- women aged 18-34 who have been affected by legislation requiring equal access to sports activities in schools --, Sports Illustrated's new sports magazine will cover both the personalities and issues of sport.

"With the growing interest in women's sports, the development of new professional leagues, and the vast numbers of women who participate in and actively watch sports, we feel the timing for this magazine is perfect," said Sports Illustrated Associate Publisher John Jay.
Over the past five years Sports Illustrated's female readership has grown by 15 percent to more than 5 million.
The April issue will feature more than 100 pages. It will be slightly larger and use heavier stock paper than a regular issue of Sports Illustrated.
Initial distribution will include Sports Illustrated's 450,000 female subscribers. The newsstand cover price will be $2.95.

Sports Illustrated, published by Time Inc., has a weekly readership of about 23 million. Other Sports Illustrated ventures include SI Presents, the magazine's custom-publishing division; SITV, the television programming and production arm; SI For Kids, a monthly magazine targeted to kids age 8 and up; and CNN/SI, the 24-hour sports news and information network.
